newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian rubber ends up but trading stays dull.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian rubber ends up but trading stays dull.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed higher but trading remained dull on a lack of buying interest, dealers said.
The lower value of rubber futures in Tokyo also did not help sentiment on the local market, they said.
"There've been no changes since morning...the market is just drifting," said a trader.

At the close, December RSS1 buyer was quoted at 321 cents ($1.27) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board, up half cent from Wednesday. December SMR 20 buyer was one cent higher at 310 cents a kg.
Trading houses maintained Wednesday, quoting the SMR CV at 364 cents a kg, SMR L at 344, SMR 5 at 321, SMR 10 at 310, SMR 20 at 309 and drum latex at 235.
"The prices are just technical adjustments," said another dealer. "There is no real buying interest."
The INRO five-day moving average rose to 244.84 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Nov 6 from 243.38 on Nov 5. The daily indicator price rose to 245.17 from 244.85.
